item.title: MPPI-Generic: A CUDA Library for Stochastic Trajectory Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2409.07563v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces a new C++/CUDA library for GPU-accelerated stochastic optimization called MPPI-Generic. It provides implementations of Model Predictive Path Integral control, Tube-Model Predictive Path Integral Control, and Robust Model Predictive Path Integral Control, and allows for these algorithms to be used across many pre-existing dynamics models and cost functions. Furthermore, researchers can create their own dynamics models or cost functions following our API definitions without needing to change the actual Model Predictive Path Integral Control code. Finally, we compare computational performance to other popular implementations of Model Predictive Path Integral Control over a variety of GPUs to show the real-time capabilities our library can allow for. Library code can be found at: https://acdslab.github.io/mppi-generic-website/ .
item.dc:creator: Bogdan Vlahov, Jason Gibson, Manan Gandhi, Evangelos A. Theodorou

item.title: Hessian-Informed Flow Matching
item.description: arXiv:2410.11433v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Data from physical systems often concentrate near stable states corresponding to minima of an energy function. Around these states, the curvature of the energy landscape shapes the local covariance structure of the data, which is often highly anisotropic: small perturbations around a data point raise its energy more sharply in some directions than in others. However, standard flow matching commonly connects noise to target data through isotropic conditional paths that do not explicitly follow this physical structure. We introduce Hessian-Informed Flow Matching (HI-FM), which uses the energy Hessian at each data sample to encode this local curvature in the conditional probability paths used for training. By locally linearizing energy-driven dynamics, we derive anisotropic paths that move samples toward their targets at different rates in different directions, without changing the standard flow matching objective. We evaluate HI-FM through molecular generation on Hessian-QM9 and GEOM-Drugs, using SemlaFlow as a shared backbone. With Hessians calculated offline only for the training data, across both datasets, HI-FM improves the physical and geometric quality of generated molecules while maintaining comparable chemical validity. Under a matched optimizer-update budget, HI-FM trained with only $10\%$ of Hessian-QM9 achieves lower mean energy, strain, and bond-length $W_1$ than the full-data SemlaFlow baseline. The results support local energy curvature as a useful inductive bias for flow matching.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Iliffe Sprague, Mert Can Kurucu, Riccardo Tedoldi, Alessandro Tibo, Jon Paul Janet, Hossein Azizpour

item.title: Mean--Variance Portfolio Selection by Continuous-Time Reinforcement Learning: Algorithms, Regret Analysis, and Empirical Study
item.description: arXiv:2412.16175v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study continuous-time mean--variance portfolio selection in markets where stock prices are diffusion processes driven by observable factors that are also diffusion processes, yet the coefficients of these processes are unknown. Based on the recently developed reinforcement learning (RL) theory for diffusion processes, we present a general data-driven RL approach that learns the pre-committed investment strategy directly without attempting to learn or estimate the market coefficients. For multi-stock Black--Scholes markets without factors, we further devise an algorithm and prove its performance guarantee by deriving a sublinear regret bound in terms of the Sharpe ratio. We then carry out an extensive empirical study implementing this algorithm to compare its performance and trading characteristics, evaluated under a host of common metrics, with a large number of widely employed portfolio allocation strategies on S\&P 500 constituents. The results demonstrate that the proposed continuous-time RL strategy is consistently among the best, especially in a volatile bear market, and decisively outperforms the model-based continuous-time counterparts by significant margins.
item.dc:creator: Yilie Huang, Yanwei Jia, Xun Yu Zhou

item.title: Convergence and stability of Q-learning in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2511.17351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning promises, among other benefits, to efficiently capture and utilize the temporal structure of a decision-making problem and to enhance transfer learning capabilities, but theoretical guarantees lag behind practice. In this paper, we propose a Feudal Q-learning scheme and investigate under which conditions its coupled updates converge and are stable. By leveraging the theory of Stochastic Approximation and the ODE method, we present a theorem stating the convergence and stability properties of Feudal Q-learning. This provides a principled convergence and stability analysis tailored to Feudal RL. Moreover, we show that the updates converge to a point that can be interpreted as an equilibrium of a suitably defined game, opening the door to game-theoretic approaches to Hierarchical RL. Lastly, experiments based on the Feudal Q-learning algorithm support the outcomes anticipated by theory.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Manenti and A. Iannelli, Convergence and stability of Q-learning in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning, Neurocomputing, vol. 710, p. 135319, 2027

item.title: SAGAS: Semantic-Aware Graph-Assisted Stitching for Offline Temporal Logic Planning
item.description: arXiv:2512.00775v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) provides a rigorous framework for specifying long-horizon robotic tasks, yet existing approaches face a trade-off: model-based synthesis relies on accurate labeled transition systems, whereas learning-based methods often require online interaction, task-specific rewards, or specification-conditioned training. We study LTL-specified robotic planning and execution in an offline, model-free setting, where the agent is given only fixed, task-agnostic trajectory fragments, with no dynamics model, task demonstrations, or online data collection. To address this setting, we propose SAGAS, a framework that combines the compositionality of symbolic synthesis with the data-driven reachability structure learned from offline trajectories. SAGAS first learns a reusable latent reachability graph and a frozen goal-conditioned executor from fragmented offline data. For each new LTL formula, it performs task-time semantic graph augmentation to ground state-defined propositions on the learned graph and applies B\"uchi product search to synthesize a cost-aware accepting prefix--suffix waypoint plan executed by the frozen executor. This separation of learning and planning enables zero-shot generalization to unseen LTL formulas and new predicates supported by the offline data, without task-specific rewards, additional data collection, or policy retraining. Experiments on LTL task suites constructed from OGBench locomotion domains show that SAGAS achieves higher success rates and lower execution costs than baselines on diverse unseen tasks, with further evaluation in OGBench Scene demonstrating its applicability to robotic manipulation.
item.dc:creator: Ruijia Liu, Ancheng Hou, Xiang Yin

item.title: QuantGraph: A Receding-Horizon Quantum Graph Solver
item.description: arXiv:2512.15476v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dynamic programming is a cornerstone of graph-based optimization. While effective, it scales unfavorably with problem size. In this work, we present QuantGraph, a two-stage quantum-enhanced framework that casts local and global graph-optimization problems as quantum-searches over discrete trajectory spaces. The solver is designed to operate efficiently by first finding a sequence of locally optimal transitions in the graph (local stage), without considering full trajectories. The accumulated cost of the resulting candidate acts as a threshold that prunes the search space (up to 60% reduction for certain examples). The subsequent global stage, based on this threshold, refines the solution. To achieve scalability and robustness, we draw on principles from control theory and embed QuantGraph's global stage within a receding-horizon model-predictive-control scheme. This classical layer stabilizes and guides the quantum search, improving precision and reducing computational burden. In practice, the resulting closed-loop system exhibits robust behavior and lower query complexity. Notably, for a fixed control horizon and query budget, QuantGraph supports approximately twice as many control discretization bits while still benefiting from Grover-search's inherent quadratic speedup compared to classical methods.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Vaidhyanathan, Aristotelis Papatheodorou, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur, Mark T. Mitchison, Natalia Ares, Ioannis Havoutis

item.title: ART for Diffusion Sampling: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Timestep Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2601.18681v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider time discretization for score-based diffusion models to generate samples from a learned reverse-time dynamic on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted grids can be suboptimal given a budget on the number of time steps. We introduce Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), which controls the clock speed of a reparameterized time variable to redistribute computation along the sampling trajectory while preserving the terminal time, with the objective of minimizing the aggregate Euler discretization error. We derive a randomized companion ART-RL that recasts ART as a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem with Gaussian policies, and prove a two-directional bridge between the two: the deterministic ART optimum lifts to an optimal Gaussian policy, and conversely any optimal Gaussian policy must recover the ART control through its mean. This bridge turns continuous-time actor--critic learning into a principled, rather than heuristic, route to the deterministic timestep optimum. Within the official EDM pipeline, ART-RL improves FID on CIFAR--10 across a wide range of budgets; after one-time offline training, the distilled deterministic schedule transfers without retraining to AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet at no extra inference cost.
item.dc:creator: Yilie Huang, Wenpin Tang, Xun Yu Zhou

item.title: Strategically Robust Linear Quadratic Dynamic Games
item.description: arXiv:2604.22318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study linear quadratic dynamic games where players are uncertain about each other's control policies or goals and consequently seek to be strategically robust. Building on recent work on strategically robust and risk-averse game theory, we first formalize the problem of strategically robust linear quadratic dynamic games. We show that these can be rewritten as simple transformations of linear quadratic games in which each player chooses a controller in a fictitious game in which they are faced with an adversary who is penalized for deviating from the other players' policies. This formulation naturally induces a novel notion of dynamic equilibrium, which we call a strategically robust dynamic equilibrium. We establish existence and uniqueness (in the subgame-perfect sense) of such equilibria and show that the equilibrium policies are Markovian, linear, and can be efficiently computed via coupled backward Riccati equations. Through numerical simulations, including experiments in a network game, we illustrate the benefits of strategic robustness in designing robust and resilient decentralized control schemes. Our experiments also expose a "free-lunch" phenomenon in games in which robustness does not incur a corresponding loss in performance but can yield improvements in players' utilities and social welfare.
item.dc:creator: Boris Velasevic, Nicolas Lanzetti, Eric Mazumdar

item.title: Equation-Free Digital Twins for Nonlinear Structural Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2605.00950v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Monitoring floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs) under stochastic excitation and sensor failure requires computationally efficient and physically interpretable estimators. This paper introduces an equation-free, output-only digital twin framework combining Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel-DMD), sparse-sensor reconstruction, and a stochastic Kalman extension. A sufficient identifiability condition is derived for modal amplitudes recovered from delay-embedded measurements, while Tikhonov regularization addresses ill-conditioned sensor layouts. Correlation-domain identification improves damping estimates under stochastic forcing and distinguishes structural modes from rotor harmonics. The framework is validated using OpenFAST simulations of an NREL 5-MW spar turbine and experimental basin-test measurements from a 1:70-scale IEA 15-MW semi-submersible. In simulations, the identified tower modes agree with established operational modal analysis methods (MAC at least 0.99), while the Kalman estimator achieves R-squared values of 0.91 to 0.99 under severe sensor sparsity. Experimental results identify tower modes at 0.430 and 0.415 Hz with MAC of 1.00 against SSI-COV and reconstruct tower-base bending moments on unseen runs with R-squared values of 0.83 to 0.89 using three of four sensors. The framework provides a computationally efficient, sensor-failure-resilient structural-state estimation layer for digital twins.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Mahdi Abaei, Ahmad BahooToroody, Arttu Poloj\"arvi, Heikki Remes, Ulf Tyge Tygesen, Mikko Suominen, Michael Beer

item.title: Policy Library CBF: Finite-Horizon Safety at Runtime via Parallel Rollouts
item.description: arXiv:2605.16588v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Safety-critical autonomy in unstructured environments poses significant challenges for online safety certification under evolving constraints, particularly when a single backup policy is not effective across operating conditions. We propose the Policy Library Control Barrier Function (PL-CBF), a runtime safety filter that evaluates a library of fallback policies via parallel finite-horizon rollouts. Among policies with constraint-satisfying rollouts and feasible CBF constraints, PL-CBF selects the policy maximizing the volume of its admissible control set and solves a single quadratic program to minimally modify the nominal input within that constrained input set. Using a finite-horizon language metric over closed-loop behaviors, we characterize when a finite policy library contains a constraint-satisfying rollout. Five simulation studies cover indoor robot navigation with a double-integrator model (4 states), highway driving under abrupt friction changes with a nonlinear vehicle model (8 states), and quadrotor flight control among dynamic obstacles (12 states), demonstrating improved safety performance compared with the evaluated baselines while maintaining millisecond-scale mean computation times. Hardware experiments on a mobile robot among moving pedestrians and a custom-built quadrotor among dynamic obstacles demonstrate real-time operation of PL-CBF.
item.dc:creator: Taekyung Kim, Hideki Okamoto, Bardh Hoxha, Georgios Fainekos, Dimitra Panagou

item.title: On-Device Robotic Planning: Eliminating Inference Redundancy for Efficient Decision-Making
item.description: arXiv:2605.31460v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reasoning-based robotic policies using large language and vision-language models achieve strong semantic planning capabilities but mostly suffer from a high inference latency that limits practical real-time deployment. In this work, we observe that robotic reasoning workloads contain substantial temporal redundancy, where consecutive observations frequently produce identical actions and subgoals. Based on this insight, we present REIS, a human cognition inspired robotic decision-making framework that minimizes unnecessary reasoning while preserving semantic adaptability. REIS combines lightweight scene gating, KV-steered affordance routing, and deliberative reasoning to accelerate robotic control under embodied constraints. Experiments on ALFRED, and real-world robotic tasks demonstrate that REIS significantly suppresses reasoning overhead while maintaining competitive task performance
item.dc:creator: Joonhee Lee, Sungmin Lee, Hyunseung Shin, Hyunmi Kim, Pei Zhang, Jeonggil Ko

item.title: Learning-enabled Acceleration of Scenario-based Model Predictive Control
item.description: arXiv:2607.12775v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scenario-based model predictive control (SBMPC) is a variant of model predictive control (MPC) that explicitly accounts for uncertainty by optimizing control actions over multiple predicted scenarios. However, its computational complexity increases rapidly with the number of scenarios and prediction horizon, limiting its applicability to real-time planning and control. This paper presents a learning-accelerated Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) algorithm for efficiently solving SBMPC problems by leveraging parallel computing and Moreau envelope learning, while maintaining high solution accuracy. We reformulate the SBMPC problems into consensus forms that can be decomposed via ADMM, separating the scenario-dependent dynamics from non-anticipativity constraints and enabling parallel updates across scenarios and time steps. Building on this decomposition, we utilize a learning-to-optimize scheme that leverages Moreau envelope learning of the cost function to accelerate the primal update in ADMM, thereby reducing computation time. The proposed framework is evaluated on a microgrid energy management problem subject to load and renewable generation uncertainties. Comparisons with IPOPT and MadNLP, two popular and modern nonlinear programming solvers, demonstrate substantial computational speedups while maintaining reliable closed-loop control performance.
item.dc:creator: Trinh Tran, Binh Nguyen, Truong X. Nghiem

item.title: Physics-informed Learning for Orbital Uncertainty Propagation with Error Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2609.01881v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Fokker-Planck partial differential equation (FP-PDE) governs uncertainty evolution in stochastic dynamical systems. In orbital dynamics, solving the FP-PDE is challenging because of nonlinear motion, high-dimensional states, and large space-time domains. We develop a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach that approximates the FP-PDE solution as a single space-time probability density, while also quantifying its worst-case approximation error. This approach is, in principle, independent of the choice of state coordinates and neural network architecture. Specifically, to enforce probability density function (PDF) properties into the neural network, we design a Physics-informed Gaussian mixture model (PINN-GMM). Then a companion error PINN learns the dynamics of the approximation error and yields time-dependent bounds that define an ambiguity set of PDFs. This ambiguity set enables rigorous computation of upper and lower bounds on event probabilities through tractable linear programs. Numerical studies on illustrative 1D examples and several 4D--6D orbital test cases demonstrate accurate uncertainty propagation, correct and informative error bounds, and improved reliability over common uncertainty-propagation baseline methods (Gaussian approximation, unscented transform, and Gaussian mixture model). Constructing the PINN-GMM requires offline training, making it costlier than the baseline approximations; once trained, however, a single forward pass returns the density at any time in sub-millisecond time $(0.16~\mathrm{ms}$ in our implementation).
item.dc:creator: Chun-Wei Kong, Morteza Lahijanian, Jay McMahon

item.title: From Grid to Chip: Power Architecture, Stability, and Flexibility of AI Data Centers
item.description: arXiv:2609.11649v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) computing is transforming data centers into large, dynamic electrical loads. Their deployment is primarily constrained by energy availability and grid-connection capacity, which is further aggravated by the ability of power-delivery architectures, control systems, and computing workloads to operate reliably during fast grid disturbances. This article provides a comprehensive overview of forefront challenges and trends in the grid-to-chip framework, and presents a technological perspective on AI data centers as grid-interactive computing systems. First, it reviews grid-integration bottlenecks, evolving connection policies, grid-code requirements, which has fostered new technological trends via spatio-temporal flexibility available through workload orchestration, cooling systems, on-site resources, and energy storage. Second, it maps the evolution of power-delivery architectures from medium-voltage grid interfaces to chip-level, discussing higher-voltage DC distribution, solid-state transformers, wide-bandgap devices, advanced chip-level power delivery, and liquid cooling. Third, it establishes a three-level stability framework spanning rack-level DC-bus dynamics, facility-level converter interactions, and system-level grid-coupled behavior. The framework connects dominant instability mechanisms, including constant power load effects, impedance interactions, forced oscillations, and operating-mode transitions, with suitable modeling, assessment, and mitigation approaches. Synthesizing these topics, this article highlights grid-to-chip co-design as a central requirement for scalable AI infrastructure, linking computing workloads, power-delivery systems, energy buffers, and grid operation.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Song, Rui Kong, Takuro Umihara, Pooya Davari, Frede Blaabjerg, Subham Sahoo

item.title: Benign Geometry and Distributional Robustness of $\mathcal{H}_2$ Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2609.24421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study standard and distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem of a stabilizing state-feedback controller for discrete-time linear time-invariant systems. Without requiring a nonsingular disturbance controllability Gramian or a positive-definite control penalty, we establish that stationarity of a stabilizing gain in standard $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis is equivalent to global optimality and derive an exact Pythagorean identity for the performance difference. We then generalize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem by considering i.i.d. disturbances with zero mean and uniformly bounded second moments, and extend the stationarity-optimality equivalence to the corresponding distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis. Moreover, we show that every standard $\mathcal{H}_2$-optimal gain is simultaneously optimal for every such distributionally robust problem. Finally, we specialize the framework to Frobenius, Kullback--Leibler, and Wasserstein-2 ambiguity sets and obtain explicit characterizations of their worst-case covariances, which, in turn, provide performance certificates for a common optimal controller.
item.dc:creator: Arman Sharifi Kolarijani, Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani, Tam\'{a}s Keviczky, Mohamad Amin Sharifi Kolarijani

item.title: Dynamic Programming for A Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.18630v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider an infinite-horizon discounted dynamic programming (DP) problem for a countable-innovation belief-state model. The model is a surrogate for a linear-Gaussian dual control problem involving an unknown parameter vector and Gaussian observation noise. The surrogate preserves the first two moments of the Gaussian innovation and the resulting posterior second-moment structure. We allow unbounded belief and control spaces and nonnegative stage costs with quadratic growth in the posterior mean and covariance. Using a posterior-moment weight, we show that the Bellman operator is a contraction in a weighted sup-norm space. We characterize the optimal cost as the unique solution of the Bellman equation in this space, establish the existence of optimal stationary policies. We further prove weighted sup-norm convergence of value iteration, policy iteration, and optimistic policy iteration under vanishing approximation errors. The convergence results under vanishing approximation errors rely on general weighted sup-norm contraction properties and are applicable beyond the particular dual control problem considered here.
item.dc:creator: Ying Wang, Yuchao Li, H{\aa}kan Hjalmarsson

item.title: The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22189v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Romano, Ole Morten Aamo

item.title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.34128v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Benchmark and phantom experiments evaluate the framework in surgical phase recognition, target tracking under occlusion and entity overlap, and autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.
item.dc:creator: Enduo Zhao, Fangzhou Li, Yujie Zhu, Sicheng Lu, Fang Chen, Longfei Ma, Hongen Liao

item.title: Sub Terahertz LEO Satellite Communication: Is Doppler Shift a Major Challenge?
item.description: arXiv:2611.01264v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate the impact of Doppler frequency shift on sub-terahertz low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications using OFDM transmission. To comprehensively evaluate the severity of the Doppler shift impact on sub-terahertz satellite-to-ground links, we first put together an evaluation framework that jointly accounts for major Doppler-induced and non-Doppler-induced signal impairments in such systems. We then compare and contrast three possible engineering approaches to deal with Doppler shift in such a communication system. Our study concludes that (i)~while just ignoring the Doppler effect in such high-frequency and high-mobility systems substantially compromises the performance and reliability, (ii)~most of the negative effects can be eliminated by implementing only a small set of low-complexity measures. We particularly show that even a single Doppler shift estimation over a 5-min-long satellite pass over the ground user location may be sufficient to ensure high performance throughout the entire connectivity period. Hence, while Doppler shift is an important effect to account for in sub-terahertz LEO satellite communications, it should not constitute a critical design challenge for these emerging systems.
item.dc:creator: Seongjoon Kang, Parisa Ramezani, Ki Won Sung, Vitaly Petrov

item.title: Reliable and explainable analysis of AVS/RS by Statistical Model Checking and Process Mining
item.description: arXiv:2611.14371v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automated Vehicle Storage and Retrieval Systems (AVS/RS) are increasingly adopted to boost warehouse throughput while containing operational costs. We present a tool-supported analysis workflow that combines discrete-event simulation, Statistical Model Checking (SMC), and Process Mining (PM) techniques to quantify and explain AVS/RS performance. SMC, implemented through the MultiVeStA tool, delivers statistically reliable estimates of key indicators, such as cycle times and inventory consolidation, across alternative stocking and picking policies with user-specified confidence levels. MultiVeStA orchestrates multiple independent simulations in a black-box manner, enabling automated verification. PM ingests the resulting event logs to uncover the behavioural patterns and bottlenecks that drive those indicators, closing the interpretability gap typical of simulation studies. We instantiate the framework on a new open-source AVS/RS simulator configured according to recent industrial guidelines and evaluate multiple control strategies and different scenarios. Results show that the coordinated use of SMC and PM supports both predictive what-if analyses and post-hoc diagnostics. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of a combined SMC-PM workflow to AVS/RS operations, complemented by a reusable open-source simulation and analysis toolchain.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Guerrazzi, Andrea Vandin
